source_refs.note: Topic 21.4 with Quick Check 21.3, answered (PDF 82-84); equations are condensed and the amine series and silver nitrate test redrawn. The quaternary salt is named tetraethylammonium bromide. Answers need review.

blocks.text: Hydroxide ion is both a good nucleophile and a good base, so a halogenoalkane can give substitution or elimination products, depending on the conditions. The reactions are done at higher temperature under reflux, to avoid losing volatile products. Bromoethane gives ethanol with aqueous sodium hydroxide and ethene with sodium hydroxide in ethanol:

blocks.alt: Displayed bromoethane + NaOH, with 'aqueous' over the arrow, gives displayed ethanol + NaBr.
blocks.caption: Substitution reaction: bromoethane and aqueous sodium hydroxide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 82).

blocks.alt: Displayed bromoethane + NaOH, with 'alcohol' over the arrow, gives displayed ethene + HOH + NaBr.
blocks.caption: Elimination reaction: bromoethane and sodium hydroxide in alcohol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 82).

blocks.text: The cyanide ion is a strong nucleophile but a weak base, so it gives substitution: a nitrile. The halogenoalkane is heated under reflux with potassium cyanide in ethanol. Bromoethane gives propanenitrile: CH3CH2Br + KCN -> CH3CH2CN + KBr.

blocks.alt: Displayed bromoethane + K+ -C(triple bond)N, with 'alcohol' over the arrow, gives displayed propanenitrile, H3C-CH2-C(triple bond)N, + KBr.
blocks.caption: Bromoethane and potassium cyanide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 82).

blocks.text: Ammonia is a good nucleophile and reacts with halogenoalkanes heated in ethanol under pressure: C2H5Br + NH3 -> C2H5NH2 (ethylamine, ethanamine) + HBr. Different amines can be obtained by carefully controlling the amounts used.

blocks.alt: Ammonia, with a lone pair on N, and a curly arrow from N to the carbon of C2H5-Br; a curly arrow from the C-Br bond to Br. The arrow gives ethylamine, H2N-C2H5, + HBr (hydrogen bromide).
blocks.caption: Ammonia and bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 82).

blocks.text: The amine formed is itself a nucleophile and competes with ammonia, so further substitution gives N-ethylethanamine, (C2H5)2NH, then N,N-diethylethanamine, (C2H5)3N.

blocks.alt: Ethanamine (N with C2H5, two H and a lone pair) with curly arrows from N to the carbon of C2H5-Br and from the C-Br bond to Br, giving N-ethylethanamine + HBr (hydrogen bromide).
blocks.caption: Ethanamine and bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 83).

blocks.alt: N-ethylethanamine (N with two C2H5, one H and a lone pair) with curly arrows from N to the carbon of C2H5-Br and from the C-Br bond to Br, giving N,N-diethylethanamine + HBr (hydrogen bromide).
blocks.caption: N-ethylethanamine and bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 83).

blocks.text: With a large excess of bromoethane the final product is the quaternary ammonium salt, tetraethylammonium bromide, (C2H5)4N+ Br-.

blocks.alt: N,N-diethylethanamine (N with three C2H5 and a lone pair) with curly arrows from N to the carbon of C2H5-Br and from the C-Br bond to Br, giving the quaternary salt: N with four C2H5 groups in square brackets with a positive charge, and Br- outside the brackets.
blocks.caption: N,N-diethylethanamine and bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 83).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed quaternary salt puts Br- inside the bracket of the positive ion and names it 'N,N,N-triethylethanaminebromide'; it is [(C2H5)4N]+ Br-, N,N,N-triethylethanaminium bromide, as drawn above.

The reaction is done in a mixture of water and ethanol; the ethanol helps the halogenoalkane dissolve. Water acts as a nucleophile and replaces the halogen: CH3CH2X + H2O -> CH3CH2OH + H+ + X-. The halide ion released then reacts with silver nitrate to give a precipitate whose colour shows which halogen was present.
